newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares at new high in record volume.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares at new high in record volume.

text.p: Istanbul shares rose an average 1.12 percent in record turnover on Friday, with the index hitting a fifth all-time closing high in a row.
The IMKB-100 ended at 91,758.91, up 1,018.05 points from Thursday's previous all-time high of 90,740.86, but fell from an afternoon high of 93,058.51 on profit-taking.
Non-stop gains totalled 5.49 percent this week after 5.38 percent last week. In dollar terms, the index stood at $0.9, compared to a record of $1 on April 8 and $0.67 at end-1995.
Trade volume surged to a record 35.89 trillion lira ($352.6 million) from Thursday's 21.66 trillion ($212.6 million). The previous highest turnover was 31 trillion lira on November 21.

"The index retreited from 93,000 resistance, but the uptrend remains strong. We may have a pull back to 89,000-90,000 range. A subsequent rise may carry the index to 96,000-97,000 levels," said Dilek Akdemir from Yatirim Finansman securities.
Brokers said the market would watch the results of a Treasury bill auction expected next Tuesday and November inflation data to be announced next Wednesday.
